svg.title: Requests, checks, decisions and later withdrawal
svg.desc: Visitor and Museum make contact and state what they want. Museum requests an age answer, permission to keep that answer for up to twenty-four hours, separate permission to keep an admission record and permission for marketing contact. Visitor requests operating evidence and access conditions. Each authenticates the other Entity and its request before sharing information beyond the authentication minimum. Visitor permits the age answer for admission and retention for up to twenty-four hours, and separately permits a minimal admission record for up to twenty-four hours, but refuses marketing. Museum permits its operating evidence. Visitor checks that evidence and the access conditions. If Visitor accepts them, Visitor sends the authorized age answer. Museum checks the answer and admits Visitor if the admission condition is met. Each keeps its own minimal Receipt. Either Entity can later withdraw a Grant it gave. The example shows Museum changing permission at its controlled source and rejecting further access even when notice was missed. Arrows show what depends on what, not required network messages.
svg.text: Checks come before sharing beyond the authentication minimum
1. Make contact: each states what it is and what it wants
Each decides whether it needs anything from the other.

g.text: 2. Request age answer and separate permissions
Declare purpose, data use and how long records will be kept
3. Request operating evidence and access conditions
Declare intended use and retention
4. Each authenticates the other Entity and its request
Only the authentication minimum is shared at this stage.
5. Age answer: entry; keep up to 24 hours
Admission record: permitted for up to 24 hours.
Visitor refuses marketing contact.
5. Museum permits operating evidence
Access waits for the admission check.
6. Museum's authorized operating evidence
Visitor checks the evidence and access conditions.
7. If Visitor accepts, Visitor sends the authorized age answer
Museum checks that item as Verifier.
8. Museum grants access if evidence is sufficient
Visitor enters only if Museum's evidence and conditions are acceptable.
9. Each keeps a minimal, trustworthy Receipt
Only actual checks and decisions; sharing needs permission.
Failed checks or unmet conditions: withhold information or decline
Continue only if the remaining conditions and permissions allow it.
Later withdrawal
Either Entity can withdraw a Grant it gave.
Shown: Museum changes permission at its controlled source.
Visitor requests access again
Access rejected despite old Grant or missed notice
The stages show what depends on what, not a required message sequence.
